mainTopic: Liability for offering outside the עזרה: wine and water libations, leftover blood (שירי הדם), and bird offerings
overview: This amud deals with offering things outside the עזרה. First the גמרא finishes explaining an argument about pouring a libation outside. One view says it depends on whether נסכים were offered in the מדבר. רבינא says it depends on whether ניסוך המים can be learned from ניסוך היין. A ברייתא then teaches that pouring three לוגין of wine outside brings liability, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון adds that this is only if the wine was sanctified in a כלי. רב אדא בר רב יצחק says they argue about the overflow above the rim of the measuring vessel. רבא בריה דרבה says they argue about whether נסכים were brought on a private במה, and the גמרא traces this back to רבי and חכמים and then to רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא on the פסוק ״כי תבאו״. Next, רבי יוחנן explains that רבי נחמיה, who makes one liable for leftover blood offered outside, holds שיריים מעכבין. A ברייתא seems to refute him, but the גמרא answers by splitting inner leftover blood from outer leftover blood. The amud ends with a new משנה about a bird offering that was pinched or slaughtered and then offered outside.

steps.title: The dispute depends on whether libations were offered in the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: An explanation of the earlier dispute: it hinges on whether נסכים were brought in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about whether libations were offered in the wilderness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing one explanation of the earlier argument about pouring a libation outside the עזרה. That argument, it says, comes down to whether נסכים were brought in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides are not arguing directly about the libation itself. Their disagreement rests on a historical-halachic question: were wine libations part of the service in the משכן in the מדבר? The גמרא will explain later how this question connects to liability outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Libations, liquid offerings poured on the מזבח
The wilderness, the period of the משכן before entering ארץ ישראל
They disagree

phrases.english: They disagree about whether libations were offered in the wilderness.
phrases.notes: This finishes an explanation from just before this point. 'They' are the two sides of the argument about pouring a libation outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation, begun on the previous page, of the root of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute depends on whether נסכים were offered in the מדבר.

steps.title: רבינא: the dispute is whether water libation is learned from wine libation
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains the dispute differently: the question is whether ניסוך המים can be derived from ניסוך היין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: They disagree about whether the water libation is learned from the wine libation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different explanation of the same argument. He says everyone agrees about wine, and the real question is whether water is treated the same way as wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבינא's view, both sides agree that someone who pours wine outside is liable. They argue only about water. One side derives the liability for pouring water from the liability for pouring wine. The other side does not make that derivation.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn or derive one law from another
The water libation poured on the מזבח on סוכות
The wine libation brought with offerings

phrases.english: Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּלְמֵדִין נִיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם מִנִּיסּוּךְ הַיַּיִן פְּלִיגִי.
phrases.english: They disagree about whether we learn the water libation from the wine libation.
phrases.notes: He means: is someone who pours water outside liable just like someone who pours wine outside?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the same dispute explained in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is whether ניסוך המים is derived from ניסוך היין for liability outside.

steps.title: ברייתא: pouring three log of wine outside, and whether it must be sanctified first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that pouring three לוגין of wine outside makes one liable. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון adds that this is only when the wine was sanctified in a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who pours three log of wine outside is liable. רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says: only if he sanctified it in a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about pouring wine outside the עזרה. It records two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא states the basic rule: three לוגין is the amount that creates liability for pouring wine outside. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון adds a condition: the wine must first have been sanctified in a כלי שרת. On the surface they seem to argue about whether sanctification is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Log, a liquid measure; three לוגין is the wine libation for a ram
Outside the עזרה, where offering is forbidden
He sanctified them in a sacred service vessel

steps.confusionAlert: The plain wording suggests the תנא קמא does not require sanctification in a כלי, but the גמרא gives two readings. רב אדא בר רב יצחק (step 5) says both require it and they argue only about the overflow. רבא בריה דרבה (step 6) says they really do argue about whether a נסך that was never sanctified in a כלי brings liability.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: הַמְנַסֵּךְ שְׁלֹשָׁה לוּגִּין יַיִן בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: One who pours three log of wine as a libation outside is liable.
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
And that is only when he sanctified them in a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic with a ברייתא about pouring wine outside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pouring three לוגין of wine outside makes one liable. According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, this applies only if the wine was sanctified in a כלי.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the actual difference between the two opinions in the ברייתא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the two opinions actually disagree about in practice. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks for the concrete case where the two opinions reach different rulings. Two different answers follow: one in step 5 and one in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what practical case do the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reach different rulings?

steps.title: רב אדא בר רב יצחק: they differ about the overflow of the measuring vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר רב יצחק answers that the difference concerns בירוצי מידות, the liquid that overflows the rim of a measuring vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר רב יצחק said: The overflow of the measures is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר רב יצחק answers the question. The two sides disagree about the wine that rises above the rim of the measuring vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that liability requires sanctification in a כלי. They argue about whether the overflow above the rim is also sanctified. For the תנא קמא it is, so pouring three לוגין of it outside creates liability. For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון only the wine inside the walls of the כלי counts as sanctified.

keyTerms.meaning: The overflow that heaps above the rim of a measuring vessel
There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אדא בר רב יצחק, both sides in the ברייתא agree that wine poured outside makes one liable only if it was sanctified in a כלי. Their only dispute is whether the overflow above the vessel's rim (בירוצי מידות) counts as sanctified. Step 6 gives a different explanation.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון mentions 'sanctified in a vessel', רב אדא בר רב יצחק says both sides require it, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is only excluding the overflow. רבא בריה דרבה in step 6 reads the dispute differently.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Rav Yitzchak said:
The overflow of the measuring vessels is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: This is the wine that heaps up above the rim of the measuring cup. The question is whether that part is sanctified too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical difference is the overflow above the rim of the measuring vessel. The תנא קמא holds it is sanctified, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds it is not.

steps.title: רבא son of רבה: the difference is whether נסכים were brought on a private altar
steps.stepSummary: רבא בריה דרבה offers another answer to the question of step 4: the two views in the ברייתא differ over whether wine נסכים were offered on a במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא son of רבה said: the difference between them is whether wine libations were offered on a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer to the question 'what is the difference between the two views?' רבא בריה דרבה says it comes down to whether נסכים were offered on a במה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At a private במה no כלי שרת were used. So if נסכים were brought there, a נסך can count even without being sanctified in a כלי, and one would be liable for pouring it outside. If נסכים were never brought on a במה, there is no example of a valid נסך without a כלי, and that supports רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: An altar outside the מקדש, used at times when such altars were allowed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רב אדא בר רב יצחק's answer in step 5 about overflowing liquid. This is a completely different explanation of the same argument.

phrases.english: Rava, son of Rabba, said:
whether libations were offered on a private altar
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה אָמַר: קָרְבוּ נְסָכִים בְּבָמָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the question of step 4, alongside רב אדא בר רב יצחק's answer in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the practical difference between the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ over whether נסכים were offered on a private במה, where no כלי was used.

steps.title: The argument of רבי and חכמים about libations on a private altar
steps.stepSummary: The argument about נסכים on a במה is the known argument of רבי and חכמים: רבי says a במת יחיד does not need נסכים, and חכמים say it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows the dispute of these תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: a private altar does not need libations; these are the words of רבי. And חכמים say: it does need libations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא בריה דרבה's point is not new. It matches an older argument between רבי and חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that a קרבן on a private altar comes without נסכים. חכמים hold it needs נסכים. So the question of whether one is liable for pouring wine outside without a כלי ends up depending on this argument.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar used by one person
A dispute or argument
Requires

phrases.english: And it is in the dispute of these Tannaim,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
A private altar does not need libations.
These are the words of Rabbi.
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: it does need libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds רבא בריה דרבה's explanation in an older argument between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: a במת יחיד does not need נסכים. חכמים: it does need נסכים.

steps.title: Linking to another ברייתא: ״כי תבאו״ speaks of the great altar
steps.stepSummary: The argument of רבי and חכמים matches another argument between תנאים, which starts with a ברייתא reading ״כי תבאו״ as requiring נסכים on the great public במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these תנאים are like those תנאים, as it is taught: 'When you come': the verse speaks to require libations for the great altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes one level deeper and connects the רבי and חכמים argument to an even older ברייתא. It begins quoting that ברייתא, which explains the פסוק ״כי תבאו״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the פסוק about נסכים starting 'when you come' to ארץ ישראל is about the great public altar. That assumes the public altar in the מדבר did not have נסכים, which links back to step 1. It also suggests the פסוק is not teaching נסכים for a private במה.

keyTerms.meaning: The great public altar used by all of ישראל
To require it to have
The פסוק is speaking about

phrases.english: And these Tannaim are like those Tannaim,
phrases.notes: 'These' are רבי and חכמים from the last step; 'those' are the תנאים in the ברייתא about to be quoted.

phrases.english: as it is taught: "When you come":
to require it to have libations,
the verse speaks of the great altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי כְּהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי – דְּתַנְיָא: ״כִּי תָבֹאוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the רבי and חכמים argument to an earlier argument between תנאים about how to read ״כי תבאו״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״כי תבאו״ teaches that נסכים are required on the great public במה once ישראל enter the land.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל proves from ״לכם״ that the verse means the public altar
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the פסוק might mean even a small private במה. It answers that the plural wording, 'which I give to you all', shows it means the altar used by everyone. This is the view of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it means the great altar; or perhaps it means even a small altar? Since it says 'into the land of your dwellings which I give to you', the verse is speaking of the altar used by all of you. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a question is raised: maybe the פסוק means a private altar? רבי ישמעאל proves from the plural wording of the פסוק that it means the public altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לכם, 'to you' in the plural, points to something shared by the whole nation, which is the public altar. So in רבי ישמעאל's view, this פסוק does not require נסכים on a private במה, which fits רבי's opinion. The words 'דברי רבי ישמעאל' tell us another תנא's view is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: A small, private altar
A ברייתא formula: 'You say this, or perhaps it means that?'
That is used by all of you

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base reading that the chain of steps 6-8 depends on. It shows how the question of liability for pouring wine outside reaches all the way back to how a פסוק is read.

phrases.english: You say it refers to the great altar;
or perhaps it refers even to a small altar?
When it says:
"Into the land of your dwellings
which I give to you,"
phrases.notes: The key word is לכם, 'to you' in the plural, meaning the whole nation together.

phrases.english: then it is about an altar used by all of you
that the verse speaks.
These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לְבָמָה גְּדוֹלָה; אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֲפִילּוּ בָּמָה קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, defending its reading against the idea that the פסוק means a private altar.
steps.raayaObject: That ״כי תבאו״ requires נסכים only on the great public במה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plural word לכם in ״אשר אני נתן לכם״ (במדבר 15:2), which points to an altar shared by everyone.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא reads the verse as adding libations to a small altar
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי עקיבא says the פסוק ״כי תבאו״ comes to require נסכים on a small private במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: the verse 'When you come' is speaking about requiring libations for a small altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the second opinion. רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל about which altar the פסוק is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל said the פסוק adds נסכים to the big public במה. רבי עקיבא says it adds נסכים even to a small private במה. Each opinion reads the same words in a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: "When you come" (במדבר 15:2), the opening words of the פרשה about נסכים

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
"When you come" —
to require libations
for a small altar
phrases.notes: Some versions say בבמה, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is לבמה. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing תנא's reading of the same פסוק that רבי ישמעאל explained in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, ״כי תבאו״ requires נסכים on a small private במה.

steps.title: Proof from 'the land of your dwellings' that a private altar is meant
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether רבי עקיבא's פסוק might mean the big במה. It answers that ״ארץ מושבתיכם״ points to an altar found in every place people live, which must be a private במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it means a small altar, but maybe it only means the great altar? When it says 'to the land of your dwellings,' the verse is talking about an altar that is used in all the places where people live.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests רבי עקיבא's reading by suggesting the other option. Then it proves his reading from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was only one big public במה at a time, so it could not be found 'in all your dwellings'. An altar found everywhere people live must be the small private במה. This mirrors how רבי ישמעאל proved his own reading from different words in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only
Your dwellings; the places where you live

phrases.english: You say it means a small altar;
or is it only for the great altar?
When it says:
"to the land of your dwellings" —
then it is about an altar that is in use
in all dwelling places that the verse is speaking.
phrases.notes: An altar found everywhere people live can only be a private one, since there was just one public altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לְבָמָה קְטַנָּה; אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְבָמָה גְּדוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי עקיבא's reading from step 10 against the other option.
steps.raayaObject: That ״כי תבאו״ refers to a small private במה, according to רבי עקיבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words ״אל ארץ מושבתיכם״, meaning an altar found in all places of dwelling

steps.title: The result: did the Jews offer libations in the desert?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the result. According to רבי ישמעאל, no נסכים were offered in the desert. According to רבי עקיבא, they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out that according to רבי ישמעאל, libations were not offered in the desert, and according to רבי עקיבא, libations were offered in the desert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up what each reading means for the time in the desert. This ties the ברייתא back to the question of whether נסכים were brought in the desert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק has to add נסכים to the big במה once they enter the land, as רבי ישמעאל says, then there were none in the desert before that. If the פסוק only adds the small במה, as רבי עקיבא says, then נסכים were already brought on the big altar in the desert.

keyTerms.meaning: When you work it out, you will find; it turns out
According to the words of
Were offered
In the desert, before entering ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל: the פסוק adds נסכים to the big public במה, so there were no נסכים in the desert. רבי עקיבא: the פסוק adds the small private במה, so נסכים were already brought in the desert.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the two readings of ״כי תבאו״ lead to a real difference in history and הלכה, which links this ברייתא to the earlier argument about נסכים on a במה.

phrases.english: When you work it out, you will find:
according to the words of Rabbi Yishmael —
libations were not offered in the desert,
and according to the words of Rabbi Akiva —
libations were offered in the desert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the two readings in steps 9-11 mean for the desert period.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי ישמעאל holds there were no נסכים in the desert. רבי עקיבא holds there were.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: liability for leftover blood offered outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. רבי נחמיה says that if someone offered the leftover blood outside the Temple, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: if someone offered the leftover blood outside, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of נסכים and quotes the next opinion in the משנה. This sets up a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leftover blood is normally poured at the base of the altar after the main sprinkling. רבי נחמיה treats offering it outside the Temple as a punishable act, even though it is only the leftover. The גמרא will now look into this view.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood that remains after the main sprinkling
Liable to punishment

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says:
the leftover blood
which one offered outside —
he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: שְׁיָרֵי הַדָּם שֶׁהִקְרִיבָן בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נחמיה, one who offers שירי הדם outside the Temple is liable.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains the reason behind רבי נחמיה's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי נחמיה's ruling follows the view that the leftover blood is essential to the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי נחמיה taught his ruling according to the one who says the leftover blood is essential.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the reason for רבי נחמיה's ruling from the last step. He says רבי נחמיה must hold that pouring the leftover blood is essential to the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would someone be liable for offering just the leftover blood outside? רבי יוחנן says it is because רבי נחמיה holds שיריים מעכבין. If the leftover blood is essential, pouring it counts as a real part of the service.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood that remains after the main sprinklings; it is poured on the base of the altar
Holding back, being essential: without it the offering does not work

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Rabbi Neḥemya taught
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: according to the one who says the leftover blood is essential.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי נחמיה's ruling in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נחמיה's liability for leftover blood offered outside is based on the view that שיריים מעכבין.

steps.title: A ברייתא where רבי עקיבא questions רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבי נחמיה makes one liable for leftover blood offered outside, and רבי עקיבא objects that it is only a leftover part of the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection: רבי נחמיה says that if someone offered leftover blood outside, he is liable. רבי עקיבא said to him: But leftover blood is only the leftover part of a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge to רבי יוחנן by quoting a ברייתא. This step quotes the start of a debate, and the real question will come out in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא argues that pouring the leftover blood is not a main part of the service. It is only the tail end of a מצוה. So offering it outside should not make a person liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover part of a מצוה, not the essential part

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Neḥemya says:
the leftover blood that one offered outside, he is liable.
Rabbi Akiva said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא שְׁיָרֵי הַדָּם שְׁיָרֵי מִצְוָה הֵם!
phrases.english: But isn't the leftover blood just the leftover part of a מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that will be used against רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי נחמיה holds שיריים מעכבין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's debate will show how רבי נחמיה defends his view, and that defense will reveal what he holds.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה brings proof from limbs and fats
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה answers that limbs and fats are also leftover parts of a מצוה, yet one is liable for offering them outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Limbs and fats will prove it. They are a leftover part of a מצוה, and yet one who offers them outside is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה defends his ruling by pointing to a case everyone agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limbs and fats of an offering are also not essential, because the offering already works through the blood. Still, burning them outside makes a person liable. So being a leftover מצוה does not free someone from liability.

keyTerms.meaning: The limbs of the animal that are burned on the altar
The fats burned on the altar
Will prove it

phrases.english: He said to him:
limbs and fats will prove it,
since they are the leftover part of a מצוה,
and one who offers them outside is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי נחמיה answers רבי עקיבא's objection.
steps.raayaObject: That leftover blood offered outside brings liability
steps.raayaSupportSource: Limbs and fats, which are not essential but still bring liability outside

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: limbs and fats are a service of their own
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the proof: burning limbs and fats starts a new service, but pouring leftover blood does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. You can say that about limbs and fats, because they are the start of a service. Can you say it about leftover blood, which is not the start of a service?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back on רבי נחמיה's proof and shows the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning limbs and fats is its own separate act of service. Pouring the leftover blood is only the end of the blood sprinkling that already happened. So the proof from limbs and fats does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: The start of a service: an act of service that stands on its own
If you said (this about one case), can you say it about another?

phrases.english: He said to him: No;
if you said it about limbs and fats,
which are the start of a service,
will you say it about leftover blood,
which is not the start of a service?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי נחמיה's proof from step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between limbs and fats and leftover blood
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Limbs and fats are a new service of their own, but leftover blood only finishes the sprinkling.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי נחמיה say the leftover blood is essential?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that if רבי נחמיה held שיריים מעכבין, he would have answered רבי עקיבא with that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so, let him say to him: These too are essential!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא makes its actual challenge against רבי יוחנן, using the debate it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי נחמיה really held that leftover blood is essential, he had an easy answer: it is essential, so it is a real service. He did not say that, which suggests he holds it is not essential. That goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so (if your claim were true)
Let him say to him

phrases.english: And if it is so,
let him say to him:
these too are essential!
phrases.notes: "These" means the leftover blood. רבי נחמיה could have said it is essential, so it is a real service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא's debate to attack רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נחמיה's silence about שיריים מעכבין, when that would have won the argument, shows he does not hold it.

steps.title: A strong refutation of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares the challenge a conclusive refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the challenge against רבי יוחנן stands. Step 20 will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא means the statement is knocked down. For the moment, רבי יוחנן's explanation of רבי נחמיה seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now, the ברייתא refutes רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Inner leftover blood versus outer leftover blood
steps.stepSummary: Using רב אדא בר אהבה's teaching, the גמרא says the משנה is about inner leftover blood and the ברייתא is about outer leftover blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And now that רב אדא בר אהבה said: The argument is about inner leftover blood, but about outer leftover blood everyone agrees it is not essential. When רבי נחמיה speaks in the משנה, it is about inner leftover blood. When that ברייתא is taught, it is about outer leftover blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a later teaching that saves רבי יוחנן after all. The משנה and the ברייתא are talking about two different kinds of leftover blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה says the question of whether leftover blood is essential only applies to blood from offerings sprinkled inside. In the ברייתא, about outer blood, רבי נחמיה could not say "it is essential," because everyone agrees it isn't. In the משנה, about inner blood, he can hold שיריים מעכבין, just as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: And now (now that we know a new teaching)
Inner: from offerings whose blood is sprinkled inside the Sanctuary
Outer: from offerings whose blood is sprinkled on the outer altar
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן stands. In the משנה, רבי נחמיה is talking about inner leftover blood, which may be essential. The ברייתא is about outer leftover blood, which everyone agrees is not essential.
steps.confusionAlert: The word תיובתא in step 19 is not the last word. The "והשתא" here shows that, with רב אדא בר אהבה's teaching, the problem is answered.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: And now that Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
the dispute is about the inner leftover blood,
but about the outer leftover blood,
everyone agrees they are not essential;
when Rabbi Neḥemya says it,
phrases.notes: This is his ruling in the משנה, from step 13.

phrases.english: it is about the inner leftover blood;
when that one is taught,
phrases.notes: "That one" means the ברייתא with רבי עקיבא from steps 15 to 17.

phrases.english: it is about the outer leftover blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undoes the refutation of step 19 by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (inner versus outer leftover blood)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא are about the same leftover blood, so רבי נחמיה cannot hold שיריים מעכבין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about inner leftover blood, where רבי נחמיה holds it is essential. The ברייתא is about outer leftover blood, which everyone agrees is not essential.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא misunderstood which leftover blood רבי נחמיה meant
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא thought רבי נחמיה was talking about outer leftover blood, so he answered about outer blood. רבי נחמיה replied within רבי עקיבא's way of seeing things, so he never brought up שיריים מעכבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא did not understand what רבי נחמיה meant. He thought רבי נחמיה was talking about leftover blood from the outer altar, so he answered about outer leftovers. רבי נחמיה then answered him in line with how רבי עקיבא had understood him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the inner/outer split from Step 20 to explain the conversation in the ברייתא. It also answers the question from Step 18: why רבי נחמיה never said 'leftovers are essential.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה was really talking about inner leftover blood, which he holds is essential. רבי עקיבא heard it as outer leftover blood, which is not essential. Since רבי עקיבא's reply was about outer blood, רבי נחמיה argued from limbs and fats on that same ground and did not raise the inner-blood point.

keyTerms.meaning: did not know / did not understand
leftover blood from offerings whose blood goes on the outer altar
answers him back
according to his (the other person's) words or view

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's back-and-forth is a misunderstanding. רבי נחמיה meant inner leftovers, which are essential. רבי עקיבא heard outer leftovers, which are not essential. So the challenge from Step 18 is answered.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי נחמיה gave up his view that inner leftovers are essential. He simply argued inside רבי עקיבא's framing and never needed to raise it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This undoes the refutation of רבי יוחנן (Steps 18-19). The משנה and the ברייתא no longer clash, because each is talking about a different kind of leftover blood.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva did not know
what Rabbi Nechemya was saying;
he thought:
Rabbi Nechemya is speaking about outer leftovers,
and so he answered him about the outer leftovers.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה – לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא קָאָמַר.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Nechemya was speaking according to Rabbi Akiva's words.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לָא יָדַע מַאי קָאָמַר רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies Step 20's inner/outer split to the dialogue in the ברייתא and answers the challenge from Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the dialogue as a misunderstanding
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי נחמיה held leftovers are essential, he should have said so to רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא thought the topic was outer leftovers, so רבי נחמיה answered on those terms. Raising inner leftovers' essential status would not have fit that conversation.

steps.title: New משנה on a bird offering pinched or slaughtered and then offered outside
steps.stepSummary: Three cases. Pinched inside and offered outside: liable. Pinched outside and offered outside: exempt. Slaughtered inside and offered outside: exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone pinches a bird offering inside the courtyard and offers it up outside, he is liable. If he pinched it outside and offered it outside, he is exempt. If he slaughtered the bird with a knife inside and offered it outside, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out when offering up a bird outside the Temple courtyard makes a person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability depends on how the bird was killed. Only a bird pinched the proper way, by מליקה inside, brings liability when offered outside. A bird pinched outside, or slaughtered with a knife inside, leads to an exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: pinching the back of a bird offering's neck with the כהן's fingernail, the way bird offerings are killed
offered it up (burned it as an offering)
inside / outside the Temple courtyard
liable / exempt
one who slaughters with a knife

steps.confusionAlert: With animals, slaughtering is the normal method. With bird offerings, the normal method is pinching (מליקה). So 'slaughtered inside' here does not mean the bird was done properly.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who pinches the nape of a bird offering inside
phrases.notes: 'Inside' means inside the Temple courtyard. 'Outside' means outside it.

phrases.english: and offered it up outside is liable.
If he pinched outside and offered it up outside, he is exempt.
One who slaughters a bird offering inside
and offered it up outside is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹלֵק אֶת הָעוֹף בִּפְנִים וְהֶעֱלָה בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic: bird offerings offered outside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pinched inside and offered outside: liable. Pinched outside and offered outside: exempt. Slaughtered inside and offered outside: exempt.
